clue.text: Fruit produce helping jam firm

parts.note: read as a description: a substance that fruit yields and that makes preserves set

explanation.surface: A note on how fruit makes jam set properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the natural gelling agent in fruit that sets jam when boiled with sugar.

clue.text: In which all one's prospects go up in smoke?

definitions.text: In which all one's prospects go up in smoke?

parts.words: In which all one's prospects go up in smoke
parts.note: the smoke suggests ruin by fire, but the image is of an opium smoker's idle fantasy of the future

explanation.surface: Someone's hopes all going up in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the hazy visions of opium smokers, so a hopeless fancy literally goes up in smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrealistic hope or fantasy, named after opium-induced visions, never comes to anything.

clue.text: Note the girl in charge is exemplary

parts.note: C is a musical note
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A note says the girl in charge sets a fine example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something classic is a model of its kind, a standard to be copied.

clue.text: It's entered by mistake and so attracted attention

indicators.note: letters put in by mistake are put in the wrong order, so these words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something got entered in error, and that made people notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that interested you caught and held your attention.

clue.text: He's killing! — takes fools in

parts.note: a fool is an ass; the plural gives two of them
the second ass from the plural fools

explanation.surface: A dramatic cry: he is murdering people, and taking idiots in as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fools' supplies two asses side by side; 'takes' only joins, and IN is the clue's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer is someone engaged in killing, typically by a planned attack.

clue.text: Withdraws clause, we hear

definitions.meaning: a horse that is pulled out of a race is struck off the list of runners
the word clause sounds like claws, which as a verb means to tear at with nails

explanation.surface: Someone takes back a contract clause, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works through a sound: 'clause' heard as claws, and to claw is to rake with the nails.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out of a race or contest is the horse-racing sense; claws as a verb means to scrape with nails.

clue.text: The voice can vary a lot

indicators.note: letters that can vary may be put in a different order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the human voice changes a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a singing voice, the lowest female or highest male range.

clue.text: Plant everything in turn

indicators.note: everything goes in, placed inside the word for a turn

parts.note: a shot is a turn or go, as in 'have a shot'
all means everything

explanation.surface: Instructions to plant everything one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like vegetable grown as a garden crop.

clue.text: She gets up fairly late in the morning

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters climb, so the phrase is read bottom to top

parts.note: at ten, meaning ten in the morning, is fairly late to rise

explanation.surface: A woman who lies in bed until the morning is well advanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' defines a girl's name; 'at ten' (o'clock in the morning) written upward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Netta is a woman's given name, so it can stand for any she.

clue.text: Pirate put in confinement

definitions.meaning: to pirate is to copy someone's work without permission
to shut up in a small enclosed space, such as a stall or child's cot

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy work dishonestly is to plagiarise; to shut into a cramped space is to confine.

clue.text: Note added to change to get a book of David's works

parts.note: a note added to a letter is a postscript, PS
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Someone adds a note to amend things and produce a volume of the king's writings.
explanation.walkthrough: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a volume containing the Psalms, traditionally ascribed to King David.

clue.text: Take. back 'touching pamphlet

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on, as in a business letter
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: Someone recovers a moving leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw a statement or claim is to take it back.

clue.text: Share out is tried, .but goes' wrong

indicators.note: something that goes wrong ends up in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan is attempted but fails.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out is to hand out portions to several people.

clue.text: Some people always find an excuse:

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An observation that certain people always manage to come up with a pretext.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'find an excuse' is a verb phrase and cannot stand in for a noun; 'find' is a link word and 'an excuse' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is a reason offered in defence or as a justification.

clue.text: Still resembling peas in a pod?

definitions.meaning: still in the sense of nevertheless or even so
peas in a pod are proverbially identical, each one like the others

explanation.surface: Things that remain as alike as peas in a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless is one sense of the phrase; identical in every respect is the literal sense.

clue.text: Cuts trains with no hesitation

indicators.note: with no tells us to take the hesitation away from the word for trains

parts.note: to train is to exercise, as with an athlete or soldier
er is the hesitation sound in speech

explanation.surface: Railway services are cut without any pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like railway stock but is a verb meaning drills.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to remove by cutting out, as a surgeon does.

clue.text: Famed organist going round America — he keeps going

indicators.note: the organist's name goes round the abbreviation for America

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was a celebrated Victorian organist and composer of church music
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A celebrated organ player tours the States and keeps on going.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stainer, organist of St Paul's Cathedral, is best known for his oratorio The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sustainer is one who keeps something going or maintains it.

clue.text: A music man accompanying the monarch needed to carry a pistol!

indicators.note: accompanying puts the composer's name side by side with the monarch's letters

parts.note: Gustav Holst was an English composer, best known for The Planets
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A composer escorting the sovereign must be armed with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer's use rather than giving a synonym: a gun case is what you need to carry a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is the leather case worn on a belt or under the arm to hold a handgun.

clue.text: Put right when changed?

definitions.meaning: to correct or remedy a wrong
changed as in changed clothes, dressed again

explanation.surface: Was something corrected once it was altered?
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as RE-DRESSED for the second sense: someone who has changed has put clothes on again.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedying a grievance is the first sense; clothed afresh after a change of outfit is the second.

clue.text: Mess about and maybe cause great anger

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Messing around might provoke great fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MESS and AND; 'maybe cause' only links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness can mean rage or fury, as in being mad with someone.

clue.text: Refuse to be removed by him

definitions.text: Refuse to be removed by him

parts.words: Refuse to be removed by him
parts.note: refuse reads as a verb, saying no, but it is the noun meaning household rubbish taken away

explanation.surface: Someone declines to be removed by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Refuse' as the noun for rubbish (stress on the first syllable) and the clue describes the man who collects it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustman is a British word for a refuse collector, who carries away household waste.

clue.text: Children, holding races left as arranged

indicators.note: the word for children holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants, as in the biblical sense
TT stands for Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Kids having races, leaving things as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled matter has been decided or agreed.

clue.text: Type of Latin verse associated, with Pope

definitions.meaning: medieval Latin verse with internal rhyme, named after a poet called Leo or Pope Leo
relating to any pope named Leo

explanation.surface: A kind of Latin poetry connected with the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine verse is internally rhymed Latin poetry; the word also means relating to a Pope Leo.

clue.text: Tilt and roll

definitions.meaning: a ship that leans to one side is said to tilt over
a roll is a register or catalogue of names

explanation.surface: A ship pitching and rolling.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship leaning to one side does this; a register of names is the second sense.

clue.text: Public house a 26 erected in the fifties

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pieces inside the pair of fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give two Ls

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means stood upright, so the letters read upward

parts.note: 26 refers to the answer at 26 down, meaning a business; a business is a company, CO

explanation.surface: A pub, one of 26, built in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns A and CO upward to give OCA, which sits between the two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a British term for the pub nearest one's home, the one regularly visited.

clue.text: It's.an engagement party — note the' racket!

parts.note: a military engagement is a battle
a do is a party or celebration
re is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An announcement of an engagement celebration, and what a noise!
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' and 'racket' suggest a betrothal party and noise, but they are a fight and a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is the small bat used in the old game of battledore and shuttlecock.

clue.text: Put in order that's quite considerable

definitions.meaning: fairly large, as in a sizeable sum of money

explanation.surface: Arrange things that amount to a fair amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Straightening up is the verb sense; 'a goodly sum' is the British informal adjective sense.

clue.text: Constant concern

explanation.surface: A worry that never goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast and unchanging is one sense; a business enterprise is the other.

clue.text: A poet's bloomer.

definitions.meaning: Thomas ... was an Elizabethan poet and composer of lute songs
a bloomer is something that blooms, a flower

explanation.surface: A versifier's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a gaffe, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Campion was an English poet; campion is also a wildflower with pink or white blooms.

clue.text: More than five hundred stars have made records

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and DI is 501, one more
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Over five hundred celebrities have set new bests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' and 'records' suggest celebrities and achievements; they are a constellation and journals.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaries are daily written accounts kept as a record of events.

clue.text: Outstanding feature of British and German currency

parts.note: L stands for the British pound, from the Latin libra
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: The most notable thing about the pound and the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' serves both countries: the British currency is the pound, written L.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent feature that stands out in a landscape.

clue.text: Such a story makes a member' object

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an end is an aim or object, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A tale that makes an MP protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' and 'object' suggest a Member of Parliament raising an objection; they are a limb and a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale handed down, often not historically true.
